section_summary: A Kobe consular report examines Japan’s accelerated gold exports in late 1939, their likely effect on bank reserves, and efforts to increase gold production. Its attachments provide export tables, a finance minister’s speech and commentary, and press clippings on mining in Taiwan, Korea, Manchuria and China. The section ends partway through a compilation of clippings about gold-price premiums.

people.role: American consul at Kobe; report author

subfiles.title: Japan Speeds Up Gold Exports and Reduces Gold Bank Reserves During Latter Part of 1939
subfiles.from: L. H. Gourley, American Consul, Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports accelerated gold shipments and assesses their sources and effect on Japan’s reserves.
subfiles.summary: Gourley calculates substantial gold exports in 1939, especially a rush of shipments to the United States in December before the commercial treaty’s termination. He doubts newly mined gold alone could account for them, citing purchases from private holders and a newly disclosed reduction in Bank of Japan specie reserves. The report also discusses obstacles faced by an American mining company in Korea, prospective Taiwanese deposits, production premiums, gold-use restrictions, banknote issues and foreign trade.

subfiles.title: Attachment No. 1: Gold Exports
subfiles.about: Introduces export statistics.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet for gold-export tables.

subfiles.title: 1939 Gold Shipments to United States by Months
subfiles.from: American consular offices in Osaka, Tokyo and Kobe
subfiles.about: Lists shipment dates, weights and yen values through December 15, 1939.
subfiles.summary: Monthly consular records total 148,936,068.9 grams and ¥653,296,271.12 for 1939 through December 15.

subfiles.title: Gold Exports from Japan in 1937, 1938 and 1939
subfiles.from: American consular offices in Kobe, Osaka and Tokyo
subfiles.about: Compares annual export quantities and values.
subfiles.summary: Tabulates 1937–1939 exports, totaling 544,243,071.6625 grams and ¥2,191,147,303.

subfiles.title: Attachment No. 2: Finance Minister’s Speech on Gold Exports and Economic Matters
subfiles.about: Introduces a speech and editorial.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet for material on finance minister Kazuo Aoki’s speech.

subfiles.title: Speech of Finance Minister Kazuo Aoki on Japan’s Gold Exports and Other Financial Matters
subfiles.about: Sets out wartime financial policy and figures for trade, gold shipments, bonds and savings.
subfiles.summary: Aoki describes mobilization of finance and industry for the war in China, increased bank deposits and savings, controls on prices and speculation, and the yen’s new dollar link. He reports gold exports of ¥860 million in 1937 and ¥660 million in 1938, while advocating higher production and collection of privately held gold. He also outlines budget, taxation and government-bond financing.

subfiles.title: Speeches of Finance Minister, Governor of Bank of Japan
subfiles.about: Criticizes Aoki’s speech and compares it with Yuki’s remarks.
subfiles.summary: The editorial faults Aoki for offering little concrete guidance on inflation, commodities and future finances. It finds Bank of Japan governor Yuki more direct about production difficulties, economic controls, export finance and bond absorption.

subfiles.title: Attachment No. 3: Gold Production
subfiles.about: Introduces press clippings on gold production.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet for gold-production clippings.

subfiles.title: Discovery of New Placer Gold Deposits in Taiwan
subfiles.about: Reports potentially valuable alluvial deposits in Takkiri Gorge.
subfiles.summary: Taiwan officials report high-purity placer gold and estimate deposits exceeding ¥1 billion. They restrict public mining and plan further surveys and state operations.

subfiles.title: New Gold Deposits Found in Formosa
subfiles.about: Describes the Tatsukiri discovery and preparations for placer mining.
subfiles.summary: Tabata says gold was found in sandy ground beside a river; officials expect mining to begin the following spring.

subfiles.title: Gold Rush in Formosa
subfiles.about: Reports 92-percent-pure nuggets found in Tatsukiri Valley.
subfiles.summary: Prospectors reportedly obtained an average 13 grams of gold per cubic tsubo of sand.

subfiles.title: Island El Dorado Again Gets Notice
subfiles.about: Reviews claims about Takkiri’s gold and government exploration plans.
subfiles.summary: The article revisits Yokobori’s disputed estimate, reports official interest and planned surveys, and notes preparations for mining.

subfiles.title: Unusually Rich Veins of Alluvial Gold Reported Struck in Central East Taiwan
subfiles.about: Details Ogasawara’s discovery and proposed state exploration.
subfiles.summary: Ogasawara located gold-bearing ancient sandy strata near the Takkiri and Tausai streams. Officials estimate one hill’s deposits at ¥160 million, bar private prospecting and organize additional surveys and possible state mining.

subfiles.title: Gold Discovery in Taiwan Is Described
subfiles.about: Explains Ogasawara’s theory of gold-bearing ancient river terraces.
subfiles.summary: Ogasawara describes how surveying old gravel strata above present rivers led to placer deposits near Taroko. Taiwan officials are surveying other mountain areas using his theory.

subfiles.title: Yoritaka Says Report of Huge Gold Mine True
subfiles.about: Quotes Professor Yoritaka endorsing reports of Taiwan’s deposits.
subfiles.summary: After visiting Takkiri Valley, Yoritaka affirms the find and recounts Ogasawara’s long search for its geological source.

subfiles.title: Six Mining Experts Leave for Taiwan to Investigate Alluvial Gold Deposits
subfiles.about: Names an expert party sailing to inspect Takkiri canyon.
subfiles.summary: Six specialists leave Kobe, with a seventh to join at Moji, for a December survey.

subfiles.title: Gold Rush Starts to East Formosa
subfiles.about: Reports prospectors heading toward restricted gold fields.
subfiles.summary: Ogasawara describes difficult fieldwork while authorities guard claims and prepare mining expeditions.

subfiles.title: Taiwan Government Party of Gold Hunters Discovers Nuggets, Dust at Mt. Doyon
subfiles.about: Describes a test excavation near Takkiri.
subfiles.summary: Ishizaki’s party recovers nuggets and gold dust from soil on Mount Doyon and plans continued tests.

subfiles.title: Group to Be Named on Mining Decrees
subfiles.about: Reports a planned gold-production committee and start of Takkiri mining.
subfiles.summary: Officials plan a committee to implement mining decrees as work begins in Takkiri ravines.

subfiles.title: Formosa’s Gold
subfiles.about: Reports expected investigation funding.
subfiles.summary: The Overseas Affairs Department reportedly seeks about ¥500,000 to investigate Formosa’s alluvial deposits.

subfiles.title: Nippon Kogyo to Launch Big-Scale Gold Mining Enterprise in Chosen
subfiles.about: Describes Nippon Kogyo’s purchase and planned expansion of Korean gold mines.
subfiles.summary: After acquiring the American-operated Unzan mine, the company aims to expand plant capacity and produce ¥15 million in gold annually.

subfiles.title: Chosen’s Gold Mining Very Promising: Ono
subfiles.about: Quotes Ono on Korean mine purchases, drought and coastal gold.
subfiles.summary: Ono says Japanese interests are buying foreign-owned mines and studying southern coastal deposits despite drought-related production problems.

subfiles.title: Gold Production Boom Needed in China Affair, Ono Says
subfiles.about: Reports Ono’s assessment of Korean gold and other mineral production.
subfiles.summary: Ono describes work at acquired mines, promising southern coastal alluvial gold, and increased production of other minerals.

subfiles.title: New Firm to Mine Gold in East Manchukuo
subfiles.about: Reports formation of Mimuro Mining after surveys of 49 deposits.
subfiles.summary: Mitsui establishes a ¥300,000 firm headed by Jiro Ogata to develop eastern Manchukuo mines.

subfiles.title: Mimuro Mining Co.
subfiles.about: Reports Mimuro Mining’s establishment and expansion plan.
subfiles.summary: Mitsui buys surveyed mining areas, opens a Lungching office and considers increasing the new company’s capital.

subfiles.title: More Mitsui Mines
subfiles.about: Summarizes Mitsui’s acquisition and Mimuro Mining’s formation.
subfiles.summary: Mimuro Mining will work coal, gold and silver deposits in eastern Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Hsinking-Mined Gold to Be Increased
subfiles.about: Reports planned additions to Manchoukuo Gold Mining’s dredging fleet.
subfiles.summary: The company expects more mining ships and mechanization to increase alluvial-gold output.

subfiles.title: Manchukuo Gold Production Firm to Increase Output by Adding More Ships
subfiles.about: Reports a proposed ¥5 million output increase through new mining ships.
subfiles.summary: Three new ships should bring the working fleet to ten by the next peak mining season.

subfiles.title: Report of Discovery of New Gold Veins in China
subfiles.about: Reports gold and other ore veins near Mount Wutai.
subfiles.summary: Sub-Lieutenant Akimoto surveys suspected veins over about two kilometers; samples go for assay.

subfiles.title: Attachment No. 4: Gold Price Premium or Subsidy
subfiles.about: Introduces clippings on gold-purchase prices and production subsidies.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet for gold-price premium clippings.

subfiles.title: Finance Officials Study Gold Price
subfiles.about: Discusses raising Japan’s gold purchase price after the yen’s dollar link.
subfiles.summary: Officials consider a higher buying price to encourage mining and reduce illicit sales; the article also reports budget deliberations.

subfiles.title: The Gold Purchase Price
subfiles.about: Compares a higher gold buying price with a subsidy.
subfiles.summary: The Finance Department may subsidize newly mined gold instead of raising the purchase price.

subfiles.title: To Subsidize Gold Miners
subfiles.about: Reports a proposed subsidy of 70–80 sen per gram.
subfiles.summary: Authorities reportedly plan payments to gold-mining companies to increase production.

subfiles.title: Encouraging Gold Production
subfiles.about: Explains the newly enacted subsidy system.
subfiles.summary: The Finance Department chooses subsidies for increased output over a general rise in its gold buying price.

subfiles.title: Gold Mine Output Will Be Increased
subfiles.about: Details premium regulations tied to gold output above mine-specific quotas.
subfiles.summary: The government will compare production with 1938–39 baselines and pay graduated premiums for increases, reaching ¥2 per gram above specified quotas.
